title: Inline HTML
content:
# In general You can also use raw HTML in your Markdown, and it'll mostly work pretty well. It's great for simple customization, like changing ``the color``. ``**Markdown in HTML** sometimes _work_.``

<p>However, **Markdown in HTML** sometimes _not_.</p>

In this case, you must use _HTML tags_ to reproduce the desired look. I recommend only use HTML when it's unavoidable so your page doesn’t become a spagetti. This article is about some use cases. ==Table of contents==
  • How to use certain characters inside Markdown
  • Link to a specific part of the page
  • Embedded content
  • workshop.codes colors
----- ## How to use certain characters inside Markdown When you want to use a character inside a Markdown block that is a Markdown indicator, such as using `|` within a table, the result will be confusing, because the editor doesn't know it's not meant to be an indicator but as a character.

``` | Column | Column | Column | | -------- | -------- | -------- | | Text | Text with a "|" symbol | Text | ``` | Column | Column | Column | | -------- | -------- | -------- | | Text | Text with a "|" symbol | Text |

To make a distinction, you must specify the character as a HTML reference, like `&#UNICODE;`, where "UNICODE" is the character's code according to the standard.

``` | Column | Column | Column | | -------- | -------- | -------- | | Text | Text with a "|" symbol | Text | ``` | Column | Column | Column | | -------- | -------- | -------- | | Text | Text with a "|" symbol | Text | ----- ## Link to a specific part of the page

-

==1. mark with an id the desired part/element like this== `This is point A`

This is point A

When jumping, this will be at the top, so maybe better to hide the reference a few rows above, to be pleasing to the eye. ==2. set link to this id== (don't miss the `#` sign) `Go to point A` Go to point A Go to point A, but looks better => "-" ----- ## Embedded content ==1. Get the code== Usually platforms have a "copy embed" option, or something similar at the given content. This gives you a html code, which sometimes perfect for this website, sometimes no that much. * In most cases (DESMOS, YOUTUBE, SOUNDCLOUD, GIPHY), you only need to copy+paste the html code you get with the "copy embed" option. * But, for a few special cases, like IMGUR, you need **the normal link** to the content (not the html code), complete it with `/embed` and put this into the html code below. `https://imgur.com/17FOzH4 => "https://imgur.com/17FOzH4/embed"` ``` <iframe src="https://imgur.com/17FOzH4/embed" width="50%" height="450px" style="border:none;"> </iframe> ``` ==2. Customize the _iframe_== There are many attributes and style options you can play with, here are some notable ones. * WIDTH: Your page's width is constant, so better to define WIDTH in `%`. * STYLE= BORDER:NONE: This helps the content to blend in without any ugly margin. * ALLOWFULLSCREEN: If you want to make your youtube video handier to watch. ----- ## workshop.codes colors

### Description
      A real number constant.
      
### Return
>  float


      
### Arguments


> **Name**: NUMBER
  **Description**: A real number constant.
  **Type**: float
  **Default**: 0

### Trivia
In actions/values that expect a boolean, a `Number` acts as:
* `False` if it is equal to 0.
* `True` if it is not equal to 0.

title: Player Dealt Final Blow
content:
This event type triggers for a player when they deal the final blow, killing another player or themself, and the `Conditions` evaluate to `True`.

#### Arguments

*  [Team](https://workshop.codes/wiki/articles/team) - The team(s) checked by the event.
*  [Player](https://workshop.codes/wiki/articles/player) - The player(s) checked by the event based on slot number or hero.

#### Contextual Values

*  [Event Player](https://workshop.codes/wiki/articles/event+player) - The player that triggered the event.
*  [Event Damage](https://workshop.codes/wiki/articles/event+damage) - The amount of damage dealt by `Event Player`.
*  [Attacker](https://workshop.codes/wiki/articles/attacker) - The player dealing the final blow. In this context, it has the same value as `Event Player`.
*  [Victim](https://workshop.codes/wiki/articles/victim) - The player dying from the final blow. In the case of suicide, it has the same value as `Event Player` and `Attacker`.
*  [Event Was Critical Hit](https://workshop.codes/wiki/articles/event+was+critical+hit) - Whether the inflicted damage was a headshot.
*  [Event Ability](https://workshop.codes/wiki/articles/event+ability) - The ability used by the `Attacker`.
*  [Event Direction](https://workshop.codes/wiki/articles/event+direction) - The incoming direction from the source of damage to the `Victim`.

title: How to create an import code for your project
content:
# Overview
You've done it! You've created a cool new Workshop gamemode, you've playtested it with some friends, and you've ironed out all the bugs. Now, how do you let other people play it?

In order to share your project with other Overwatch players so that they can play it for themselves, you'll need to generate an ==import code==. An import code is a string of numbers and letters, such as `Q74P7`, which players can use to play a copy of your Workshop gamemode! More details on how to import a Workshop code can be found [in this article](/wiki/articles/how+to+import+a+workshop+code).

## Step 1: Setting up your lobby
When you create an import code, a snapshot of your entire custom game lobby is taken (excluding any players, bots, or AI) and uploaded to Blizzard's servers. Therefore, you need to make sure that all your custom game settings are set to the right values and that everything you want to share is loaded.

If you've made any developer/debug tools, specified a datacenter preference, or made any other tweaks that you don't want other players to experience, now is a good time to remove or undo those things!

## Step 2: Open the lobby settings
![An Overwatch custom game lobby with the settings button circled in red](https://cdn.workshop.codes/hdhq5d3p2e5bzqnp6u5rkxoc8078)

## Step 3: Click the "Share Code" button
![The settings page of an Overwatch custom game lobby with the "Share Code" button circled](https://cdn.workshop.codes/nf9qmp2ztgnknuiz4uojsw1e5jx4)

## Step 4: Click "Continue"
!["Share A Game Settings Code" dialog with a closed dropdown that has selected "Create a New Code". Two buttons along the bottom of the dialog read "Cancel" and "Continue"](https://cdn.workshop.codes/1a1mf8kx95ij4wa5yqgys3lslnjr)

\*Note that the other option on this screen, "Upload to Existing Code", is covered [in this article](/wiki/articles/uploading+new+content+to+existing+import+code). "Upload to Existing Code" overwrites the contents of a share code you created previously, whereas "Create a New Code" generates a brand new code.

## Step 5: Share your new import code
![A dialog shows the newly created import code, along with an option to copy the code](https://cdn.workshop.codes/iiit3u8p8cjtxmshl7nqasoqx2r8)

You have now successfully generated an import code that [others can use to play your game](/wiki/articles/how+to+import+a+workshop+code). Clicking "Copy" will copy the new import code to your clipboard (PC only) so you can share it with the world!

title: Transform
content:
## Description
Used in [Local Vector Of](/wiki/articles/local+vector+of) and [World Vector Of](/wiki/articles/world+vector+of). Specifies whether the vector should receive a rotation and a translation (usually applied to positions) or only a rotation (usually applied to directions and velocities).

## Options
- **Rotation** 
  - The resulting vector will be rotated to the new frame of reference. Use this option when the provided vector is a direction or velocity.
- **Rotation And Translation** 
  - The resulting vector will be rotated and translated to the new frame of reference. Use this option when the provided vector is a position.

title: Clip
content:
## Description

Used in [Create In-World Text](/wiki/articles/create+in-world+text). Specifies whether the text can be seen through walls or is instead clipped.

## Options
- **Clip Against Surfaces** 
  - The text may be partially or completely obscured by walls, floors, ceilings, players, or other solid objects.
- **Do Not Clip** 
  - The text will always be fully visible, even if it is behind a wall or solid object.

title: Subroutine
content:
Subroutines are a special kind of event that can be triggered manually with [Call Subroutine](https://workshop.codes/wiki/articles/call+subroutine) or [Start Rule](https://workshop.codes/wiki/articles/start+rule). They also cannot have conditions.

A maximum of 128 subroutines can be created.

#### Argument

*  `Subroutine` - The associated name of this subroutine. A name can only be selected once in a project. These names can be edited with the `Edit Subroutine Names` button on the top right of the screen.

#### Contextual Value(s)

*  Uses the same contextual value(s) as the rule that called the subroutine.
